title: Dynamic array statistics
instructorPromptText: Write a C program that asks the user for a count N, dynamically allocates an integer array of size N using `malloc`, reads N integers from the user, and computes and prints the minimum, maximum, and average values. Free the memory before exit.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program verify that `malloc` (or `calloc`) successfully allocated memory (i.e. did not return `NULL`) before accessing the array?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Memory allocation validation is a core safety standard in C; accessing a NULL pointer will cause a crash/segfault.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the program invoke `free` on the allocated pointer before exiting to prevent memory leaks?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Resource cleanup is critical in languages without automatic garbage collection, highlighting the manual lifecycle management of C.

specGateDimensions.description: Does the average calculation handle floating-point conversion to avoid truncation from integer division?
specGateDimensions.rationale: Dividing two integers in C performs truncating division. Students must cast at least one operand to `double` or `float`.

expectedDivergences.pattern: Student calls `malloc` but does not check if the returned pointer is NULL.
Student leaks memory by forgetting to call `free` on the allocated pointer.
Student divides `sum` by `N` as integers, causing the average to lose its decimal part.
Student uses `calloc` instead of `malloc` to allocate and zero-initialize memory, which is a safe alternative.
Student prints stats using a different output format than the one committed to in the spec.
